purpose: qualify a complete-future, maneuver-conditioned footprint-conflict instrument on the already completed replicated CF-R closed-loop runs

evidence_design.type: retrospective fixed-data audit with formulas and decisions frozen before their values are calculated
evidence_design.independence_boundary: this is not a fresh confirmatory experiment because the underlying runs and prior endpoint summaries have already been inspected; the future-clearance values and mitigation-gain decisions have not been calculated
evidence_design.simulator_dependency: ego and actor boxes come from HUGSIM state logs; clearance, temporal matching and decisions are recomputed outside the HUGSIM scorer
evidence_design.receiver_role: SparseDrive is the target AD whose plan response is measured, not an absolute risk oracle

requirements: each included receiver plan has exactly six finite [right, forward] waypoints at 0.5 s spacing
one ego box and exactly one actor box exist at the plan timestamp
one actor box exists at every exact plan-time plus waypoint-horizon timestamp
duplicate logged states at the same timestamp agree numerically
all four runs share the same timestamp grid and each input hash matches
the t=1.5 s ego state and constant-speed reference path agree across conditions and resets
no state is repeated, interpolated, extrapolated or tail-filled
validity_gate.failure_rule: if any requirement fails, the affected construct is rejected and no future-conflict value from an incomplete plan is used

coordinate_and_footprint_contract.state_box: [world_x, world_y, world_z, width, length, height, yaw]
coordinate_and_footprint_contract.plan_axes: SparseDrive/HUGSIM plan-pipe [right, forward] metres relative to the plan-time ego state
coordinate_and_footprint_contract.future_ego_yaw: heading of each mapped waypoint segment, beginning with the segment from the plan-time origin; carry the preceding heading only for an exactly zero-length segment
coordinate_and_footprint_contract.ego_dimensions: plan-time HUGSIM ego-box width and length, held fixed across the six predicted waypoints
coordinate_and_footprint_contract.actor_dimensions_and_pose: exact HUGSIM actor box at the matching future timestamp
coordinate_and_footprint_contract.clearance: Euclidean distance in metres between oriented two-dimensional ego and actor footprint polygons; zero means touching or overlap
coordinate_and_footprint_contract.scope_note: this audits the same plan-pipe vehicle-centre convention that drove the loop; it does not independently validate HUGSIM box truth or SparseDrive vehicle-shape semantics

common_path_stimulus_conflict.reference_path: straight constant-heading continuation at the common handoff HUGSIM ego speed, sampled at the six waypoint horizons
metrics: minimum future footprint clearance in metres
earliest time of minimum clearance in seconds
common_path_stimulus_conflict.expected_relation: slow minimum clearance < fast minimum clearance in each paired reset
common_path_stimulus_conflict.interpretation: tests whether the designed actor-speed intervention has the expected dynamic geometric conflict order while the ego path is held common; it is not an AD-response measure

target_ad_mitigation.own_plan: the six native SparseDrive final-planning waypoints from that run
target_ad_mitigation.mitigation_gain_formula: own-plan minimum future clearance minus common-reference-path minimum future clearance
target_ad_mitigation.same_maneuver_gate: the selected native planning mode at t=1.5 s must be the same across all conditions and resets
expected_relations: slow mitigation gain > fast mitigation gain in each paired reset
target_ad_mitigation.interpretation: tests whether the target AD plan increases residual geometric margin relative to the same non-reactive continuation and reacts more strongly to the stronger conflict

complete_horizon_diagnostics.decision_boundary: after t=1.5 s the closed-loop ego states have diverged, so cross-condition clearance order is descriptive and is not used as a causal acceptance criterion

replication_and_decisions.pairing: slow-run001 versus fast-run001 and slow-run002 versus fast-run002
replication_and_decisions.repeat_sensitivity: the minimum paired condition effect must exceed the maximum same-condition range across the two resets
replication_and_decisions.accepted: the complete-future gate passes; the common-path conflict order passes both pairings and exceeds repeat sensitivity; the same-maneuver gate passes; every mitigation gain is positive; and the stronger-conflict mitigation gain exceeds the weaker-conflict gain in both pairings and beyond repeat sensitivity
replication_and_decisions.down-weighted: the complete-future gate and common-path conflict order pass, but the mitigation construct is tied, repeat-sensitive, or maneuver-confounded without an opposite safety response
replication_and_decisions.rejected: the complete-future gate fails, the common-path conflict order ties or reverses in any pairing, or the SparseDrive own plan reduces future clearance relative to the common path in any run
replication_and_decisions.zero_clearance_rule: absence of a zero-clearance event is not a failure; the primary construct is continuous footprint clearance

strongest_allowed_claim: within the valid 3 s prefix of this one HUGSIM scene and two actor-speed conditions, the independently recomputed dynamic footprint instrument does or does not preserve the designed conflict order under a common ego path, and the frozen SparseDrive plan does or does not add a directionally stronger clearance response beyond reset sensitivity
forbidden_claims: physical TTC, collision probability or calibrated risk
HUGSIM boxes or dynamics match reality
SparseDrive is a correct or safe driving policy
general HUGSIM, SparseDrive or closed-loop safety credibility
